title: Media’s New Fight for Eyeballs, Profits, and Control
gist: BCG finds US media grew only 0.8% a year in real per-capita terms from 2018 to 2025, with attention zero-sum and increasingly background, while revenue and especially profits migrated to social media, gaming and streaming platforms. Video value-chain profits fell $15.6B (31%) and streaming will not offset it; the durable moat is owning the consumer's moment of choice, with AI-content abundance likely raising the premium on certified-human content.

insights.claim: US media revenues grew at a 5.4% nominal CAGR from 2018 to 2025, but only 0.8% per year after adjusting for inflation and population growth.
insights.speaker: Ernesto Pagano
insights.so_what: Media is a near-zero real-growth sector; winners must take share rather than ride market growth.
insights.quote: Adjusting for inflation and increases in population, the industry—including video, audio, social media, print, gaming, and location-based entertainment (LBE)—grew just 0.8% per year.

insights.claim: Weekly US consumer media time rose only from 85.5 to 91.4 hours between 2018 and 2025, a CAGR below 1%, and 61% of surveyed consumers say more time on one media modality means less on another.
insights.speaker: Ernesto Pagano
insights.so_what: Attention is a zero-sum budget, so any platform's gain is a direct competitor's loss.

insights.claim: Because media demand has stagnated, bargaining power in the battle for attention and budgets has shifted to consumers' first-choice platforms.
insights.speaker: Ernesto Pagano
insights.so_what: Favor aggregators that are the default starting point over content suppliers dependent on them.
insights.quote: But bargaining power lies with consumers’ first-choice platforms.

insights.claim: US consumers spent over 13 hours per day with media in 2025, but only about 3 hours (28%) was focused attention; growth in media time has come entirely from background multitasking.
insights.speaker: Ernesto Pagano
insights.so_what: Headline time-spent metrics overstate monetizable attention; ad pricing based on raw time may be inflated.
insights.quote: But only about 3 hours a day, or 28%, was focused attention.

insights.claim: Social media has captured 81% of incremental US media time since 2018, while multitasking during social media use rose from 52% to 55% between 2024 and 2025, and heavy social users multitask 1.4x more than other consumers.
insights.speaker: Ernesto Pagano
insights.so_what: Social's time gains are disproportionately low-quality background attention, a latent risk to its ad yield.

insights.claim: Focused media attention has declined slightly in recent years even as total media hours increased.
insights.speaker: Ernesto Pagano
insights.so_what: Premium for scarce focused attention should rise relative to background impressions.
insights.quote: Overall, focused media attention has declined slightly in recent years

insights.claim: Video has held about 40% of focused consumer attention every year since 2018 yet produced only 16% of US media revenue growth from 2018 to 2025, and nearly half of that came from YouTube.
insights.speaker: Ernesto Pagano
insights.so_what: Video attention is badly under-monetized outside YouTube; legacy video owners are losing the revenue race despite holding attention.
insights.quote: yet it generated only 16% of the industry’s revenue growth from 2018 through 2025—and nearly half of that came from YouTube.
insights.locator: Although the proportion of consumers’ time

insights.claim: Social media rose from 8% to 12% of total media time but generated 40% of US media revenue growth from 2018 to 2025, while gaming rose from 7% to 9% of time and delivered 19% of growth.
insights.speaker: Ernesto Pagano
insights.so_what: Social and gaming are the revenue-growth engines of US media, far outrunning their share of time.

insights.claim: Revenue per hour of media varies about 18-fold across modalities: location-based entertainment $3.47, print $0.74, gaming $0.70, social media $0.69, video $0.39, and audio $0.19.
insights.speaker: Ernesto Pagano
insights.so_what: Scarce, live, in-person experiences command premium yields; video and audio are structurally low-yield.
insights.quote: In stark contrast, video generated just 39 cents per hour, and audio delivered 19 cents per hour.

insights.claim: Revenues are shifting far more than time spent, and profits are shifting even more radically than revenues, so attention share is a poor guide to value capture.
insights.speaker: Ernesto Pagano
insights.so_what: Analyze media assets on profit pools rather than audience share.
insights.quote: While revenues are shifting more dramatically than time spent, profits are moving even more radically.

insights.claim: Profits in the US video value chain fell by $15.6 billion, or 31%, from 2018 to 2025, as streaming broke the pay-TV bundle, collapsed release windows, and kept moviegoers home.
insights.speaker: Ernesto Pagano
insights.so_what: Legacy video economics have structurally deteriorated, not cyclically.
insights.quote: profits in the US video value chain declined by $15.6 billion, or 31%, from 2018 through 2025.
insights.locator: The rise of streaming dramatically changed

insights.claim: From 2018 to 2025 US cable network profits fell $13.8 billion (about 8% a year), film studio profits fell $3.8 billion (about 7% a year), and theater profits fell $2.2 billion (about 14% a year).
insights.speaker: Ernesto Pagano
insights.so_what: Theaters show the steepest rate of decline and cable the largest absolute loss; avoid treating either as a recovery trade.

insights.claim: US streaming profits swung from a $1 billion loss in 2018 to an $8.4 billion profit in 2025, but BCG says it is no longer debatable that streaming will fail to offset profit losses elsewhere in the video value chain.
insights.speaker: Ernesto Pagano
insights.so_what: The 'streaming will replace the bundle' thesis for legacy media conglomerates is dead; video profitability may be permanently impaired.
insights.quote: It is no longer a subject for debate whether streaming profits will be enough to compensate for profit pressures elsewhere in the value chain. They won’t.

themes.theme: AI content and the human premium

insights.claim: 56% of US consumers say they prefer human-generated content over AI-generated content, even as AI-generated content is expected to become more abundant.
insights.speaker: Ernesto Pagano
insights.so_what: Human provenance may become a differentiator and a labeling/certification opportunity.
insights.quote: 56% of consumers said they prefer human-generated content.
insights.locator: AI is capable of generating content

insights.claim: Consumer willingness to pay will likely bifurcate: a long tail of cheap AI-generated content could raise the value of a trusted, certified-human content tier even if stated aversion to AI content fades.
insights.speaker: Ernesto Pagano
insights.so_what: Expect a barbell market: commoditized AI content at the low end and premium-priced human/authentic content at the top.
insights.quote: A long tail of inexpensive AI-generated offerings could increase the value of the certified-human tier of content

insights.claim: Consumers prefer trusted, authentic content driven by scarce IP and communal experiences, with 'connection' the most-cited reason for choosing live streams over recorded video.
insights.speaker: Ernesto Pagano
insights.so_what: Scarce IP, live events and community-building formats should carry pricing power.

insights.claim: Platforms that build stronger community and consumer relationships have seen combined profits grow sevenfold since 2018, led by social media platforms and followed by streaming video platforms.
insights.speaker: Ernesto Pagano
insights.so_what: Profit growth is accruing to relationship-owning platforms, not content producers.
insights.quote: have seen their combined profits grow sevenfold since 2018

insights.claim: AI can significantly improve platforms' matching of content supply to consumer demand, increasing engagement time and further entrenching platforms that control discovery.
insights.speaker: Ernesto Pagano
insights.so_what: AI recommendation capability amplifies aggregator advantage over content makers.

insights.speaker: Ernesto Pagano
insights.so_what: Distribution/discovery control trumps content ownership as the durable moat in media.
